name: Draft-Monolith
description: Draft-Monolith is a cold, windswept rocky world where thermal drafts funnel through massive canyon systems with enough force to scour the stone smooth. The thin atmosphere channels these drafts into narrow, high-velocity streams that have carved the rock into monumental pillars and arches over geological time. The solar wind, barely filtered by the meager atmosphere, has etched the exposed surfaces with delicate dendritic patterns that look almost like frozen lightning.

The drafts produce an eerie moaning that echoes through the canyons, rising and falling as temperature differentials shift with the planet's rotation. Dust devils spin in the wider valleys, sometimes reaching heights of several kilometers in the low gravity before collapsing. The sky is a deep indigo, darkening to black at the zenith even during daylight, with stars visible throughout the day.

Rising from a flat plain near the planet's equator, a formation of six perfectly rectangular monoliths stands in a precise hexagonal arrangement. Each monolith is identical in dimension, twelve meters tall and three meters wide, and composed of a material that resists all attempts at sampling. A signal emanates from the center of the formation at regular intervals, broadcasting a sequence of prime numbers that repeats every seventeen hours.

Draft-Monolith's titanium deposits and strategic location have made it a candidate for mining development, but the monoliths have triggered a scientific priority designation that restricts commercial activity within a hundred-kilometer radius. Research teams rotate through the site on six-month assignments, making incremental progress in understanding the structures while the signal continues its patient, mathematical broadcast into the void.
